title: Patek Philippe Ref 2508 in 18K YG Unpolished w/ Extract
description: The Patek Philippe reference 2508 is one of the most amazing time-only models. It is powered by the calibre 27 SC. This example, with an 18K yellow gold case, is in fantastic condition. It appears to be unpolished. It is 35mm in diameter and produced by François Borgel (Taubert Frères). The dial is features some marks, but is attractive and features non-luminous hour markers and hands. The watch comes with an Extract from The Archives. It does not come with a box. The watch was serviced by Patek Philippe in August 2025 and is running well. It was originally sold on January 26th, 1957. For those looking for an incredible mid-century Patek Philippe, this is a special watch.

title: Rolex "Puzzle" "Jigsaw" Day-Date Reference 128235 18K Everose Gold Full Set Unpolished
description: The Rolex Day-Date is one of the world’s most iconic wristwatches. It was introduced in 1956 and was the first watch to display the date, as well as the fully-spelled-out day of the week. This Rolex “Puzzle” Day-Date is one of the most desirable wristwatches on the planet. Introduced at the 2023 Watches & Wonders, the Rolex “Puzzle” (or “Emoji”/”Jigsaw”) was a watch that made the watch community astonished and excited. Nobody was certain whether the watch was a hoax or an authentic release from The Crown. This “Puzzle” Day-Date in rose gold is in outstanding condition. It is an incredible off catalog Rolex. It features a “Puzzle” calendar features 31 emojis and the days are inspirational words ("Happy," "Eternity," "Gratitude," "Peace," "Faith," "Love" and "Hope"). It features 10 rainbow baguette-cut sapphire hour indexes. The watch is powered by the Rolex Calibre 3255, with a 70-hour power reserve and a double quick-set day and date function. The case measures 36mm in diameter and approximately 43mm lug-to-lug. The watch is in excellent condition and appears to be unpolished. The watch recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar. It comes as a “full set” with the original box and papers. It was sold in 2025. For those looking for an incredible and rare contemporary Rolex, this is a grail Day-Date.

title: Patek Philippe Retailed by Cartier Reference 3468 in 18K YG w/ Extract Unpolished
description: This Patek Philippe reference 3468 is an interesting Calatrava model in 18k yellow gold. The watch features a blue sunburst dial, which is extra special due to the double-signed Cartier retailer signature. Double signed dials from Rolex and Patek Philippe are highly sought after. The case measures 33mm in diameter (39mm lug-to-lug). It is made of 18k yellow gold. The caseback features an incredible engraving. It is paired on a Cartier leather strap with 18k yellow gold deployant buckle. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch does not come with box and papers. It does come with an Extract from the Archives and was originally sold in 1969. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe 404 “World Record Seaplane Flight” in 18K YG Unpolished w/ Extract
description: This is an incredibly special Patek Philippe reference 404 with a possibly unique dial featuring unusual hard enamel sector-like hour markers in the center of the dial resembling cat whiskers and what is perhaps the most outrageous and cool '7' even seen on a Patek Philippe. In fact, on close inspection, the '7' actually appears to be a modified upside-down '2' as seen in the '12'. Beyond the spectacular three-tone Art-Deco style dial and the beautiful curved long Patek Philippe & Co. signature on the dial is the engraving on the back commemorating the flight of the French seaplane the "Croix du Sud" from Cherbourg, France to Ziguinchor, Senegal. Lieutenant de vaisseau Henri-Laurent Dalliere, a French aviation legend, presumably purchased or was given this watch upon his return to France. The watch has "Fab. Suisse" on the bottom of the dial indicating it was likely originally designated to be sent to France by Patek Philippe among with a French gold hallmark on the case. This case is 18k yellow gold and measures approximately 20mm x 35mm in diameter. The rectangular dial features a subsidiary seconds at 6 o’clock and applied numerals at the 11, 12, 1, 5 and 7 o’ clock positions. It comes with an 18 yellow gold signed Patek Philippe buckle which is later. It comes with an extract from the Patek Philippe archives and was originally sold in 1935. This watch does not include the original box and papers, has a manual-wind movement (Caliber 9’’’90 made by Patek Philippe). We do not know the service history, but it is running well

title: Patek Philippe Nautilus Reference 5980/1R-001 in 18K Rose Gold Full Set Unpolished
description: The Patek Philippe Nautilus is perhaps the most desired watch on the planet. The introduction of the model marked the first true sports watch from the manufacturer in 1976. Along with the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, it ushered in the world of integrated stainless steel watches which are adored by watch enthusiasts today. This 18K rose gold example is the reference 5980R, a remarkable flyback chronograph with date. The watch is powered by the calibre CH 28‑520 C. The case and bracelet have some wear but appears to be unpolished. The rose gold case measures 40.5mm in diameter. For those looking for a luxurious complicated sports watch, there are few superior options! The watch comes full set with box and papers from the original owner who is a boss and one of Eric’s favorite friends. Good Provenance! The date on the Certificate of Origin is from 2016. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Retailed by Tiffany & Co. Breguet Numerals Wristwatch 18K YG w/ Extract
description: The watch features a beautiful retailer signature of Tiffany & Co. It has applied-Arabic numerals with spade hands. The case measures approximately 26mm in diameter (36.5mm lug-to-lug). The watch features a caseback inscription that reads “N.M.S. to J.R. 1931”. It is a very similar design to a watch that recently sold for $292,100 , although it does not feature the engravings on the side of the case. These two watches have a movement number that is within 50 digits of one another. We do not know the service history, but it is keeping good time. It does not come with a box and papers. It comes with an Extract from the Archives from Patek Philippe. It was originally sold on September 23rd, 1930.

title: Patek Philippe “Hour Glass” Ref. 1593 in 18k Yellow Gold w/ Extract
description: This Patek Phillippe time only watch measures 25.5mm by 42mm and is made of 18k yellow gold. The reference 1593 features the sought after “hour glass” case shape. It is powered by the manually wound calibre 9””90 movement. It features a service dial which is printed. The watch does not come with a box and papers. It does come with an Extract from The Archives. It was originally sold on April 17th, 1948. We do not know the full service history, but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Reference 2552 w/ Bamboo Style Bracelet in 18K YG w/ Extract
description: This Patek Philippe reference 2552 is a special example in 18K yellow gold. The case dimensions are 36mm in diameter and 41mm lug-to-lug. The case appears to be lightly polished. It is paired on an extremely stylish 14k gold bamboo style bracelet unlike any other bracelet we have ever seen. The watch formerly belonged to James (Jim) M. O'Connor who worked at Jewel Tea Company. O’Connor was a respected executive at the company and within the U.S. coffee and tea industry throughout the mid-20th century. John F. McKieran, President of the National Coffee Association was quoted about O'Connor’s work stating “Jim O'Connor’s record as a coffee man goes back through so many years and covers so many outstanding achievements that it is almost superfluous for one to emphasize them. His career is synonymous with the most turbulent and most trying era known to the coffee industry of the United States and throughout this era Jim O’Connor’s name and personality were unfailingly in the forefront.” The watch comes from the family of the original owner. The watch does not come with a box and papers. It does come with an Extract from The Archives. It was originally sold on November 4th, 1957. We do not know the full service history, but it is running well.

title: Patek Philippe Minute Repeater Pocket Watch in 18K YG
description: This is a spectacular Patek Philippe minute repeater pocket watch. The 18K yellow gold case features a beautiful monogram on the caseback, reading “MEB”. It measures 46mm in diameter and is approximately 10mm thick. The case has been lightly polished. The watch features a beautiful gold colored dial with guilloché design and Breguet numerals. There is a small seconds sub dial at 6 o’clock and the minute repeater is activities with a lever at the 3 o’clock position. The watch comes with a chain that is approximately 14 inches in length. The watch dates to the late 1910s. It features an interior engraving dating to Christmas of 1920. To learn more about Patek Philippe pocket watches, read Charlie Dunne’s article ‘ Why Your Perspective Should Change About Patek Philippe Pocket Watches ’. The watch does not include a box or papers. An Extract was not approved. Presumably the dial was replaced by Patek Philippe during a past service. We do not know the service history but it is running well and keeping good time. For those looking for a truly remarkable Patek Philippe pocket watch, this is such a special timepiece.

title: Patek Philippe Ref 783 “Montres Golf” Retailed By Gübelin Designed by Gilbert Albert w/ Pouch & Extract Unpolished
description: The watch is uniquely stylish and it is quite apparent when looking at certain elements, such as the segmented dial, that it was created by the designer. The watch is powered by the calibre 12-400, and the case measures 39mm in diameter and 8mm in height (including the crystal). In addition, it is a double-signed dial sold by the Lucerne-based retailer Gübelin. The case back features the Poinçon de Maître key numbered 2 indicating F. Baumgartner SA, a case specialist who produced the cases many water-resistant Calatrava wristwatches, including the legendary reference 2526. While many collectors prioritize wristwatches, this pocket watch is a treasure and an absolutely mesmerizing creation from one of the watch industry’s most talented minds. This particular model is from the “Montres Golf” collection of three different models depicted in the advertisement (reference 782, reference 783, and reference 799) with integrated chains made for golfers to have in their pocket when playing golf. These golf watches became somewhat in vogue in the mid-20th century as golf became more popular and it became more widely-known that the impact of a swing could damage a wristwatch’s movement. The integrated chain allowed the golfer to clip it to their pocket for quick access to the time when on the course and also to ensure that it would not accidentally get lost. The “Montres Golf” watches also frequently came with a brown leather pouch, sometimes embossed with PATEK PHILIPPE in gold, but in the case of this watch embossed with GÜBELIN in gold. This reference 783 has an ornate wreath-like pattern on the chain and edge of the case that makes it particularly appealing. This watch came from the grandson of the original owner, who was a diplomat for Iran in the 1950s and 1960s, before the Shah was deposed, and likely was a gift to him by another diplomat. title: Patek Philippe Manta Ray Gondolo 10 Day Ref. 5100G-001 in 18K WG Full Set

The watch features a rectangular blue dial with a small seconds sub dial at 6 o’clock and a 10 day power reserve indicator at 12 o’clock. It measures 34mm by 46mm including the widest point of the case and the crown. The watch features an exhibition caseback displaying the manually wound 28-20 movement. The white gold case has been lightly polished. The watch comes with a Patek Philippe black leather strap and a 18k white gold signed pin buckle. The watch comes as a “full set” with original box and papers. It was originally sold in 2001. We do not know the full service history, but it is running well.

title: Rolex Zenith Daytona Reference 16528 in 18K YG White Dial Black Subdials Unpolished

They are incredibly wearable and distinguished as the first automatic-Rolex Daytona (powered by the Rolex modified calibre 4030 made by Zenith). The watch does not include the original box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar.

This Rolex Day-Date reference 1803 is an incredibly attractive watch with an unbelievably rare United States Merchant Marine dial. We would rather have this logo on our watch than the signature of a despot who allegedly committed patricide, honestly! These Merchant Marine Day-Dates are extremely rare and only a few are known. The dial is outstanding and features the non-Roman numeral variant. The 18K-gold case has been lightly polished in the past. It likely had a caseback engraving. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar.

title: Cartier Tank Cintrée w/ Roman Numeral Dial in Platinum
description: The Cartier Tank Cintrée is one of my favorite Cartier models and is perhaps the quintessential vintage Cartier model due to their iconic design, incredible size and rarity. The cases are very well made and among the most beautiful styles from the manufacturer. These models have grown to become highly collectible over recent years. Most vintage Cartier Tank Cintrées were produced in yellow gold. Finding a vintage example in platinum is extremely rare and special. Cartier Tank Cintrées in platinum have sold well over $350,000 at auction and are among the most desirable metal in the category. This example dates to circa 1926. It features platinum French made case. The case has been lightly polished in the past. It is an oversized model wearing large on the wrist and measures 47mm in length by 23mm in diameter. The dial features the classic Roman numerals and Breguet hands. The dial appears to be reprinted and that is extremely common for the majority of vintage Cartier wristwatches. It features the original beaded cabochon crown. It is paired on a black strap with Cartier deployant buckle. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. To learn more about the spectacular watches from Cartier, read our article My Dream Cartier Collection .

title: Rolex Frog Foot Explorer I Reference 1016 Unpolished Box & Papers
description: Introduced in 1960 an icon was born in the Rolex Explorer reference 1016. The 1016 was produced until circa 1989. The ref. 1016 marked the first Explorer with “Superlative Chronometer Officially Certified" printed on the dial. It is one of the most desired timepieces and for great reason. The 1016 is one of the purest expressions of watch design and for this reason that I am probably asked for vintage Explorer reference 1016s more than any other watch. his example features a 1.73 million serial number, dating the watch to circa 1967. It is paired on a 7206 Oyster bracelet dating to 1969 with 58 endlinks and made by Gay Frères. This example features the beautiful MK I (Mark 1) Frog Foot dial dial, and attractive warm luminous material. The case which appears to be unpolished. It features a beautiful case back engraving “IN APPRECIATION TO DONALD BECKER LAVERN ASMUSSEN DEC. 6, 1969”. For those looking for an epic Rolex Explorer reference 1016 with box and papers, this watch is an outstanding choice! To learn more about the history and evolution of the Rolex Explorer I, you can see my video and corresponding article Reference Points A Comprehensive Collector's Guide To The Rolex Explorer I . The watch comes full set with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar.

title: F.P.Journe lineSport Centigraphe Reference CT2 in 18K Rose Gold Full Set New
description: The Centigraphe Sport CTS was produced from 2014 to 2018. Collectors love the Centigraphe Sport for the sport-oriented design with incredible versatility. This example is an incredible case and bracelet are made of 18k rose gold (6N) which is incredibly comfortable and elegant on the wrist. F.P.Journe collectors love these bracelets and they are among the best quality in the industry. The case and bracelet feature the “hammered” finish which is an attractive matte finish which is much more attractive than other manufacturers. The case measures approximately 42mm in diameter. The dial features non-luminous matte 5N Gold applied numerals. It features whitened guilloché subdials in silver with red accents. These grey dial variants were recently discontinued and transitioned to a black dial variant, making this one of the final grey variants. The movement is an engineering highlight. It is powered by the calibre 1506 - a movement which is made of titanium and weighs approximately 12 grams. The lineSport Centigraphe Reference CT2 is arguably one of the most advanced chronograph models ever produced capable of timing one-hundredth of a second. The subdials feature a 1/100th of a second at 10 o'clock, a 20 second dial, and a 10-minute dial at 6 o'clock. The watch comes full set from the original owner. It is in brand new condition. The watch was originally sold in 2024.

title: Rolex Patrizzi Dial Zenith Daytona Ref. 16520 w/ Box & Papers
description: The adorned “Zenith Daytonas” are certainly among the highly desired neo-vintage Rolex models. Zenith Daytonas were produced from circa 1988 until 2000. The watch is powered by an automatic Rolex Calibre 4030, modified from Zenith. The case measures 40mm in diameter (42.5 including crown) and 47mm lug to lug. This is one of the most attractive Rolex Patrizzi Daytonas we have ever come across. It features a rich dark color on the outer ring of the registers. Rolex register rings on Daytonas with black dials from the early through middle 1990s sometimes would develop a darker tone in the subdials. This effect is often given the nickname “Patrizzi” after the legendary auctioneer Osvaldo Patrizzi, who reportedly first identified this patina. The present example is an outstanding example. It features a S serial number which dates to circa 1993. The watch comes with a reference 78390 Oyster bracelet with polished center links dating to circa 1995. The case appears to have been lightly polished in the past. For those looking for a grail Zenith Daytona, this is a spectacular watch. The watch comes with a box and papers. title: Rolex “Small Crown” Submariner Ref. 6205 Unpolished
description: The reference 6205 was introduced in 1954. It is an incredibly rare Submariner model. According to Rolex, the Submariner reference 6205 was produced in only 810 examples! It was introduced with “pencil hands”. There are two generation of dials, one being the first generation with Submariner text on the dial and the 2nd being the 2nd generation or "clean dial" absent of model’s name on the dial. It has a nice gilt dial with a warm patina. The case is 37mm in diameter (47mm lug-to-lug). The watch dates to circa 1956 with a 214,XXX serial. The case appears to be unpolished. title: Rolex Tiffany & Co. Great White Sea-Dweller Reference 1665
description: This Rolex “Great White” Sea-Dweller reference 1665 is an incredibly special watch featuring a Tiffany & Co. signed dial. . The dial features a beautiful yellow lume. It is a “Maxi” Sea-Dweller dial and was among the last examples of the legendary reference 1665 made. These examples with 6 million serial numbers have the extremely large hour markers that give them the “Maxi” moniker. I find them to be the most beautiful Great White Sea-Dweller dials. The reference 1665 models with all-white text are known as “Great White” models and the early examples are known as “Double Red” Sea-Dwellers with two red lines of text and the earliest, essentially prototype and not-for-sale, Sea-Dwellers are known as “Single Red” Sea-Dwellers with a single line of red text. The case has been polished in the past. It features a 6.7M serial dating to circa 1981. The lug-to-lug length is 47mm and it measures 40mm in diameter excluding the crown. It is paired on a later service Rolex 93150 Oyster bracelet from circa 1991 and later 501B end links. The watch does not come box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well. The watch recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar. It features a TrueDome D39 crystal.

title: Rolex MK II GMT-Master Reference 1675 Pepsi

title: Heuer Jo Siffert Mk 2 Autavia Reference 1163 on GF Bracelet Unpolished
description: The Heuer “Jo Siffert” Autavia reference 1163 is one of the most iconic and exciting vintage Heuer chronographs. The watch was famously worn by the Swiss Formula 1 driver Jo Siffert in the late 1960s - early 1970s. This example dates to circa 1969. It is in outstanding condition. The case appears to be unpolished. It is powered by the automatic calibre 11 made by Heuer-Léonidas. It measures approximately 42mm in diameter. It features the Mark 2 dial and the original Tachymeter bezel. This variant has the enlarged blue hour markers and ridged hour markers and metal hour and minute hands. It features a 141XXX serial just after the Chronomatic Siffert range. It is paired on a Heuer bracelet by Gay Freres with HLD end links dating to 1970. For those looking for an incredible vintage Heuer chronograph, the Jo Siffert is a must have. This watch does not include the original box and papers. title: Heuer Dato Carrera Reference 3147N Indianapolis Motor Speedway Indy 500
description: The Heuer Carrera is one of the legendary chronograph designs of the 20th century. Featuring stark angled lugs that were a product of the architecture of the 1960s, the present watch is notably a “first execution” and features an unpolished case. Finding Carreras from the 1960s with in great condition is extremely difficult. The reference 3147 was the first Heuer Carrera with date and this is a 3147N with the N meaning “Noir” indicating a black dial. The movement is a Landeron 189 with date and the case back is thicker on these to accommodate the thicker movement with the date. The case diameter is 36mm with a lug width of 18mm. The present example is a bit of a hodgepodge. The watch features service replacement hands with Super-LumiNova. The case has been lightly polished and it has a replacement crystal. The case back sticker is in tact. It is possible the dial was placed in the watch. Regardless, it is a very rare dial and highly coveted vintage Heuer. An Autavia model with this dial sold at Christie’s for nearly $200,000 back in 2017 . You can read more about the origins of the Carrera in the in-depth article that I wrote for HODINKEE back in 2013 . We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers.

title: OMEGA Speedmaster Reference 145.022-69 BA In 18K YG
description: A Speedmaster Reference 145.022-69 BA in 18K YG OMEGA introduced the Speedmaster in 1957, initially created for drivers in automotive racing needing to time their laps. However, the Speedmaster would reach eternal iconic status by eventually being qualified for spaceflight by NASA after an intense testing of several of the highest-grade chronographs of the 1960s. NASA selected the Speedmaster as the exclusive watch for use by its astronauts. The OMEGA Speedmaster reference 145.022-69 BA was the first OMEGA Speedmaster to be produced in 18k yellow gold. Only 30 examples were produced in total for astronauts and two were produced for President Nixon and Vice President Agnew. The next examples were given to Astronauts and are considered by many to be the grail OMEGA Speedmasters. On October 20, 2022, Wally Schirra’s personal OMEGA Speedmaster Professional BA 145.022 was sold for $1,906,954 . This example is one that was sold to the public. The 18K yellow-gold case is in has been lightly polshed. The dial is fantastic and the bezel remains in good condition. The watch is powered by the caliber 861. The bracelet is long and should fit a wrist approximately 7.1 inches. Finding an example with a long bracelet is incredibly difficult. For those looking for an epic gold Speedmaster, these are amazing watches. To learn more about the OMEGA Speedmaster, you can watch my ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Entire Lineage Of The OMEGA Speedmaster ’ video and read the corresponding article. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do now know the service history, but it is running well. title: Heuer USS Whale Carrera Reference 2447S Eggshell Dial
description: This annual watch prize tradition started in 1938 and continues to this day. L.Y. Spear, President of the Electric Boat Company (which became General Dynamics), started the Spear Foundation in 1942 with an endowment to fund the watch prize. The Spear Foundation allowed the shipmate to pick out his own watch from Mallove’s Jewelers in Groton, Connecticut. Brooks wisely selected a Carrera chronograph, but there was a catch. Navy regulations restricted external radioactive sources aboard nuclear-powered boats, so as to ensure accurate monitoring of radiation levels from propulsion systems. This watch had its tritium luminous material removed from dial and hands. An early dial was evidently selected for this purpose. This was possibly done on special order from Heuer, or by the retailer at the time of original sale. Brooks served a distinguished Navy career, including as Commander of the Sturgeon-class nuclear-powered attack submarine USS Whale (SSN-638) from 1975 to 1978, retiring with the rank of Captain. As a civilian, Brooks held important Senate-confirmed positions in government. He was appointed Ambassador to lead negotiation of two strategic arms reduction treaties between the U.S. and Russia, and served as U.S. Undersecretary of Energy for Nuclear Security, responsible for managing the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA). The watch is powered by the Valjoux calibre 72. The case is lightly polished but very strong. The dial and hands had the original tritium luminous material removed. The signed crown is original. The watch is fitted on a black leather rally strap from Abel Court with a rare signed vintage “Sun” buckle. The watch does not come with box and papers. It features a rare “No Date” dial, where the word “DATE” has been omitted in the text after ‘Oyster Perpetual’. It features an Oyster reference 93150 bracelet with period correct I3 date code dating to circa March 1984 with 580 end links that is polished, but thankfully the case appears to be unpolished. They are uncommon and a bit mysterious to some, but for those who appreciate Rolex’s historic models the Turn-O-Graph is certainly one to admire. It features a beautiful gilt dial. It features the extremely rare dial with the red depth rating and the original bezel insert which is very uncommon. It is paired on a Rolex stretch rivet bracelet dating to 1956. title: Rolex GMT-Master Reference 6542 Bakelite Bezel
description: The Rolex GMT-Master reference 6542 marked the first reference in what would go onto become one of the most celebrated timepieces across all manufacturers. The timepiece became an icon within the James Bond movie Goldfinger after being worn by Honor Blackman during her portrayal of "Pussy Galore". It is an unmistakable watch and it is seen as grail watches for collectors who understand the importance of the 1950s Rolex sports catalog. This particular example is an outstanding 6542 with a spectacular dial, vivid original Bakelite bezel, and great provenance. These Bakelite bezels have a propensity for cracks and are radioactive, and as a result many were replaced with non-luminous, anodized aluminum bezels. The colors are so unique and it makes for an out of this world aesthetic. In addition to the Bakelite bezel, the dial is very well preserved and attractive. The reference 6542 dials are often known for cracking and crazing, but this example has one of the nicest dial we have seen on any reference 6542. The GMT hand has minimal lume loss, but this is expected in a sports watch over 65 years old. The case has been lightly polished, but is very attractive and full. The watch has a 398,XXX serial dating to circa late 1958. It is 38mm in diameter (48mm lug-to-lug). It is paired on what is likely its original Swiss-made Oyster rivet bracelet with super-desirable “Big Logo” clasp and 65 end links dating to 1959. It has been in an important private collection for a number of years. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. The watch recently passed a water resistance test of 3 bar. To learn more about the Rolex GMT-Master, you can watch my ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Rolex GMT-Master' video and read the corresponding article. I selected this exact watch for inclusion in the Reference Points article and video, so that should tell you how I feel about the quality of this example.

title: Patek Philippe Breguet Numerals Tasti Tondi Ref 1463 in Steel w/ Extract & Service Papers Sealed
description: The Patek Philippe chronograph reference 1463 is one of the most important and iconic references from the manufacturer. This is a special example with stainless steel case and the incredible dial variant of applied-Breguet numerals. It is estimated that 750 examples were produced - of those it is believed approximately 15-24 were produced in steel. A stainless steel reference 1463 is certainly a grail Patek Philippe, but finding one with applied Breguet numerals is exceedingly rare. The reference 1463 was introduced in circa 1940 and remained in production until the 1960s. We are excited to share this incredible example in stainless steel dating to 1949. The two-register chronograph is powered by the calibre 13-130. These cases were produced by François Borgel (Taubert Frères). Taubert Frères is regarded as one of the most exceptional chronograph case manufacturers of all time. The reference 1463 was an innovative and sport-oriented chronograph which was the first waterproof chronograph from Patek Philippe. It measures approximately 35mm in diameter and 42.5mm lug-to-lug. The case has been polished in the past. It does not come with a box or papers. It comes with an Extract from the Archives. It was produced in 1949 and sold in 1950. The watch was serviced by Patek Philippe in 2022 and accompanies service papers. It is factory sealed. For those with a passion for important Patek Philippe models, this is a particularly special timepiece.

Mr. Whiteley's most extensive service was to the Belgian Government, for which he was consul for thirty-one years. He was an authority on international law and diplomatic history and was a member of the International committee which organized Le Congres International d'Histoire Comparee in Paris in 1900. His appointment as consul for Belgium in Baltimore came in 1916 after he had been knighted by King Leopold for services rendered the Belgian Government.” The case is made of 18k yellow gold and appears to be unpolished. The watch measures 45mm in diameter. The dial is outstanding and the watch features extremely attractive blue Breguet hands. It features “Wolf’s Teeth” gearing. title: Heuer Carrera Reference 1158CH in 18K Yellow Gold Unpolished
description: The gold gold Carrera 1158 models are considered grail chronographs. The Heuer Carrera reference 1158 is an incredibly special reference and distinguished as being Jack Heuer’s favorite watch. This example is certainly one of the best preserved examples in the world. The earliest examples feature CHRONOMATIC font on the dials. I believe there are only two known examples - it is not clear whether the dials were born in those cases. The second examples were the 1158S featuring the silver dial. The present example comes in a third series, the reference 1158CH (CH referring to the gold champagne dial). The last series were the reference 1158CHN - the CH referring to the gold champagne dial with N (Noir/black) registers. These are associated with the Ferrari racing team, although Mario Andretti actually had a 1158CH as seen in his Talking Watches video. The Carrera reference 1158CH is a particularly important model in vintage Heuer and racing history. Heuer was focused on building a relationship with the Ferrari racing team and this began in the 1970s. Jack Heuer would end up providing a purported 15 examples of the Carrera reference 1158 to Ferrari F1 drivers - including Mario Andretti. It is believed that 200 examples in total were produced across all variants. The watch features a beautiful champagne dial. The case is made of 18k yellow gold. It measures 38mm in diameter. It appears to be unpolished. The caseback is decorated with a 25 year anniversary to an employee at H. Mino & Ses Fils (A Swiss industrial company). Finding an incredible vintage Heuer Carrera is quite uncommon, and this is even more uncommon in precious metal. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers.

These watches were not made for purchase by the public, but as a way to reward Domino’s franchise owners who hit their sales targets. All these watches were originally ordered through Schlanderer and Sons in Ann Arbor, Michigan, where Domino’s has its headquarters. In the past, these watches on the secondhand market were generally the least expensive Rolex a person could purchase as few people wanted a pizza logo like this on their dial. Dealers would buy them, swap out the Domino’s dial, and polish off the case back initials. Over the last year, however, they have gained a massive following. The watch features an engraving on the back with the recipient’s initials. You can learn about these watches in our video Collector Conversation: Tom Monaghan - Founder of Domino's Pizza - on the Domino's Rolex . This version features the “tilted logo” that is the last version of Dominos’s Rolex watch with the logo on the dial. . The watch features a U^ serial dating to 1997. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch comes as a “full set” with a box, papers and hangtag. It was originally sold in 1998. We do not know the full service history, but it is running well.
